learning: If line-loss events fall and s-bend/slalom max_error drops below about 0.05 m, the footprint was the gap. If line-loss stays at 1 or more with max_error near 0.06 m, the limit is turn authority, and the next step is weight scaling or a wider wheel_track test, not more span.
notes: Iteration 3 changes only sensor_size (0.012 to 0.016 m) relative to the iteration 1 best. The controller is unchanged so the footprint effect can be isolated. Oval steering oscillation is left for a later weight test.
rationale: Iteration 1 (±0.03 m span, 0.015 m spacing, 12 mm footprint, controller kp 2.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2) is the best result so far at 337.5. It finished 13/20 oval runs, but s-bend (1/20) and slalom (0/20) still exited off-track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m and 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run. Iteration 2 showed that widening the span to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing made every track worse, so span alone is not the lever. The Builder's geometry for this iteration reverts to the ±0.03 m span and changes only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, so each footprint overlaps its neighbours and closes the dead zones suggested by the line-loss counts. I keep the controller identical to iteration 1 so the race isolates the footprint change. Oval steering_oscillation (0.31) does not affect score and would confound this test if I changed weights now, so I leave weights alone and flag the oscillation for a later iteration. Speed is not limiting (oval finished in 1.83 s), so base_speed and wheel_radius stay as they are. Expected result, which is not yet measured: line-loss events fall toward 0 to 0.5 per run and s-bend/slalom max_error drops toward 0.05 m, with oval finishes held at 13/20 or better.
